hero.heading: Circle Beverage, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built September 27, 2026, from circlebev.com, the trade press, the Conexus Indiana case study, and federal data. Every number is labeled: published, federal, or our assumption. The assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: Exact computed endpoints: $8,920.00 and $86,750.00, rounded to the nearest $5,000 for display; the rounding widens the low end, so the exact figures govern.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Cans you co-pack in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per million cans.

sliders.label: Cans in a typical production run
sliders.basis: Anchored inside published co-packer minimums. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

Cost of one line hour, people and overhead
Procured cost per can on runs where you buy the materials
sliders.basis: Low end anchored to the published price of an empty can. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Months a fixed tolling quote stands

constants.text: The federal producer price index for aluminum cans rose 10.7 percent from October 2025 to May 2026, the latest month published [[BENCHMARK]], BLS series PCU3324313324313. Next update October 15. This one is not a slider.
constants.note: When the October update lands, this page's number changes with it, whichever direction it moves.

model.formulaText: Moved per 1,000,000 cans = (1,000,000 / cans per run) × changeover hours × line rate + 1,000,000 × cost per can × 0.107 × (months / 12)
model.plainText: In words, what brand-to-brand changeovers cost across a year of runs, plus the slice of this year's can-price rise a fixed tolling quote absorbs while it stands.
model.callout: Your machines measure everything they touch. Nothing on the line measures the calendar between runs: the changeover matrix across roughly twenty brands, or the days a scheduled run waits on materials that arrive from clients. Those numbers exist in your records, unread.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: You print your method on your website, four steps ending in reassessment [[OBSERVED]].
You print which client sizes fit you, on the intake form itself: under 2 million, 2 to 5 million, 5 to 15 million, and above 15 million cans a year [[OBSERVED]].
You hold SQF, USDA Organic, and FDA registrations, a distilled spirits permit, and a B Corp certificate, and you name them all in plain words [[OBSERVED]].
You told the trade press you went from everything done by hand in 2019 to almost everything done by machines, and that one sleever tripled your daily capacity [[BENCHMARK]].
You close your method with the sentence: we only win if you win [[OBSERVED]].
